keyVerseText: Malchiram also, and Pedaiah, and Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
rootMeaning: The name מַלְכִּירָם (Malkîyrâm) derives from the Hebrew root words מֶלֶךְ (melek), meaning 'king,' and רוּם (rum), meaning 'high' or 'exalted.' Literally, it signifies 'my king is high' or 'king of exaltation,' emphasizing the sovereignty and supreme status of the king. This etymology adds a layer of royal dignity and divine exaltation beyond the simple English transliteration, highlighting a connection to the divine kingship of Yahweh, the ultimate sovereign.
usageInScripture: The word מַלְכִּירָם appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 3:18, where it is used as a proper name, Malchiram, referring to a son of King Jehoiachin of Judah. Its consistent translation as 'Malchiram' indicates that it functions primarily as a personal name rather than a common noun, preserving its royal connotation in the historical genealogical record. This singular occurrence underscores the importance of the name within the Davidic lineage and its theological implications.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מַלְכִּירָם as 'my king is high' enriches our appreciation of the Davidic line's connection to God's sovereign rule. It reminds believers that earthly kingship is ultimately subordinate to the exalted reign of Yahweh, who is the true King above all. This name, borne by a descendant of Jehoiachin, points forward to the Messianic hope rooted in God's promise to David's house. It affirms that faith in God's supreme kingship is foundational to the identity and destiny of His people, encouraging trust in His sovereign plan through Christ, the exalted King.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 3:18, Malchiram is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin, anchoring him within the royal genealogy. The presence of this name in the verse highlights the continuity of God's covenantal promise through the Davidic line. The meaning 'my king is high' enriches the verse by reminding readers that these descendants are under the authority of the exalted King, Yahweh, whose reign surpasses all earthly powers. This reflection invites believers to see their own place within God's sovereign kingdom.
